name: Security
blurb: Every control a request meets, outside in: what the edge drops, what the origin lock demands, what the token is allowed to prove, and what IAM permits once the request is inside. The permissions boundary at layer 3 is the reason the private API exists at all.
audience: Security review, assurance and threat modelling
note: Two gaps are real and unfixed. pnpm validate:integrations filters to type: "domain", so only 6 of the 36 declared integrations are checked — the 30 gateway integrations pass CI unexamined, including local-council's two, which point at /v1/local-council/* routes the udp gateway does not define. And the authorizer's allow policy names Resource: "*" rather than the invoked method ARN.

d.role: Everything a request meets before it leaves the edge network.
facts: One distribution per stage. The Web ACL, the viewer-request function and the response-headers policies all live in this stack because CloudFront requires us-east-1.

d.role: Proves the request came through CloudFront, then proves who is asking.
facts: The origin lock and the token check are independent: passing the Web ACL says nothing about identity, and a valid token reaches nothing without the origin header.

d.role: What a route function is allowed to reach once it is running.
facts: Three independent constraints have to agree before one function can reach another: the VPC endpoint condition on the API, the permissions boundary, and the route's own inline policy.

d.tech: Secrets Manager · KMS · CDK Aspect · Powertools logger
d.role: What protects the material the controls above depend on.
Edge filtering for the distribution.
facts: Priority order: 0 AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet · 1 AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet · 2 BypassForE2ETests (allow) · 3 AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList · 4 RateLimit, block above 2000 per IP.
Rule 2 is an exact byte match on the x-flex-e2e-bypass header against a generated secret. Because it is an allow it terminates evaluation and skips rules 3 and 4 — but 0 and 1 have already run.
Data protection substitutes the authorization header in WAF logs, sampled requests and rate-based details.

nodes.label: Viewer-request CloudFront Function
nodes.sub: JS 2.0 · token shape only, no signature

d.role: Rejects malformed bearer tokens before the request leaves the edge.
facts: Fails on: missing Authorization header, no Bearer prefix, extra header segments, wrong JWT segment count, header or body that is not JSON, and alg: none. The signature is only checked for presence — never verified.
A rejection is a 401 carrying x-rejected-by: cloudfront-function; success emits cff_token_validated.
It also sets x-correlation-id, keeping the inbound value only if it is a v4 UUID. The /docs* behaviour runs a different function that only rewrites URIs.

d.role: DDoS protection, where it is created at all.
facts: #createCloudfrontShield early-exits when the environment is development, so the development environment and every ephemeral and personal stage have no protection and no DDoS alarms.
Application-layer automatic response is ENABLED with action count — attacks are evaluated and reported, not mitigated automatically.

nodes.label: CloudFront distribution
nodes.sub: TLS 1.2_2021 floor · HSTS · injects the origin secret

d.role: The single public entry point, and where TLS terminates.
facts: Viewer TLS floor is SecurityPolicyProtocol.TLS_V1_2_2021. The API behaviour is HTTPS_ONLY; /docs* is REDIRECT_TO_HTTPS.

Response headers on both behaviours: HSTS 365 days with includeSubdomains, X-Frame-Options: DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies: none. The API behaviour adds default-src 'self' and Cache-Control: no-store.
It adds the x-origin-verify custom header to every request it forwards to the API origin — that header is the entire origin lock.

nodes.label: REGIONAL Web ACL
nodes.sub: default BLOCK · 2 rules · on the public stage

d.role: The origin lock on the public API stage.
facts: The default action is block, which is what makes the raw execute-api URL unusable: rule 1 is the only thing that lets a request through.
Rule 0 is KnownBadInputs; rule 1 RequireOriginSecret is an EXACTLY byte match on the x-origin-verify single header with no text transformation.
sampledRequestsEnabled is false on the origin-secret rule, so the header value is never captured into sampled requests.

d.role: Where the authorizer is attached and where auth failures become status codes.
facts: securityPolicy: SecurityPolicy_TLS13_1_2_2021_06, set on the L1 resource rather than through the L2 props.
Two gateway responses are overridden: 401 UNAUTHORIZED and 403 ACCESS_DENIED, both rendering $context.authorizer.errorMessage as JSON.
Each domain stack attaches its own TokenAuthorizer over the shared authorizer function, and only if that domain has public routes.

nodes.label: Cognito token authorizer
nodes.sub: Lambda · egress tier · asserts one claim

d.role: Turns a bearer token into one asserted identity, or a deny.
facts: Verifies issuer https://cognito-idp.{region}.amazonaws.com/{USERPOOL_ID}, token_use: access and the client id. audience is deliberately null, because Cognito access tokens carry none.
The only thing it asserts downstream is pairwiseId, taken from the token's username claim and returned in the authorizer context. principalId is the constant string anonymous.
Deny is scoped to event.methodArn. Expired tokens carry the message JWT expired; every other failure denies with no message. The 401 fires only when API Gateway rejects before the authorizer runs.
Gap: the allow policy is returned with Resource: "*" instead of the invoked method ARN, so a single successful verification authorizes every method on the API.
The verifier is constructed inside the handler, so the three environment variables are Zod-parsed on every invocation.

d.tech: Hosted UI federating to GOV.UK One Login
d.role: Issues the access tokens FLEX verifies. FLEX never sees One Login itself.
facts: USERPOOL_ID and CLIENT_ID are imported from /{env}/flex-param/auth/*; the development environment uses the separate stub pool and client parameters instead.
In production the JWKS URI is built as https://cognito-idp.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/{userPoolId}/.well-known/jwks.json; development points it at a stub JWKS Function URL created in the platform stack.

nodes.label: Route Lambda and its execution role
nodes.sub: one generated role per route function

d.tech: NodejsFunction execution role under the boundary
d.role: The identity every internal call is made with.
facts: Every route function gets its own generated role. The only hand-written roles in the app are the API Gateway CloudWatch role and {env}-flex-smoke-test-role, the one role with an explicit physical name.

Calls to the private API are SigV4-signed with the function's own execution-role credentials. Only the UDP and UNS gateways swap in assumed-role credentials, granted per gateway as sts:AssumeRole on one named role ARN and cached for the STS hour.
ctx.auth.pairwiseId exists on public routes only; a private route has no ctx.auth at all and takes identity as a declared header if it needs one.

nodes.label: Private REST API
nodes.sub: PRIVATE endpoint · IAM auth on every method

d.tech: EndpointType.PRIVATE bound to the API Gateway interface endpoint
d.role: The only sanctioned path from one FLEX function to another.
facts: The resource policy holds a single statement: Deny execute-api:Invoke for AnyPrincipal whenever aws:SourceVpce is not that one endpoint.
There is no explicit Allow, so for same-account callers the caller's own IAM policy is the sole gate — which is exactly what the boundary and the per-route policy below are for.
AuthorizationType.IAM is the default method option, so every method requires a signed request, /health included.

d.role: A hard ceiling on every role in the stack it is applied to.
facts: DenyDirectLambdaInvoke — Deny lambda:InvokeFunction on *. No FLEX function can invoke another directly. This single statement is the reason the private API design exists.
AllowFlexPrivateApiInvoke — execute-api:Invoke scoped to arnForExecuteApi("*", "/*", "*") on the private API alone, so no role can reach a different API even if its inline policy grants it.

Four baseline Allows on *: logs (3 actions), X-Ray (2), the five ENI actions, and service integrations — Secrets Manager read and describe, six SSM parameter actions including PutParameter and DeleteParameter, kms:Decrypt and sts:AssumeRole. CKV_AWS_107/108/111 are suppressed with recorded reasons.
One policy in the platform stack and one per deployed domain stack. Roles created in the core, global, deploy and smoke-test stacks are not under a boundary.

d.role: Turns each route's declared integrations into least-privilege IAM.
facts: A route function's inline policy lists only the route ARNs that route's own integrations array names, grouped by method, with SIDs AllowApiAccess{Domain}{Method}.
Domain integrations resolve to /domains/{target}/{version}{path} and gateway ones to /gateways/{target}/{version}{path}. The stage segment is left as *.

Gap: validateDomainIntegrations filters to type: "domain", so only 6 of the 36 declared integrations are validated. The 30 gateway integrations are never checked against a real gateway route — which is how local-council's two calls to /v1/local-council/* on the udp gateway reach CI intact and 404 at runtime.

d.role: Holds the two values the edge controls compare against.
facts: /{stage}/flex-secret/origin-verify-secret is created in eu-west-2 and replicated to us-east-1; /{stage}/flex-secret/waf/e2e-bypass the other way round. Both use AWS managed keys with a recorded CKV_AWS_149 suppression so replication stays simple.

Both are resolved by CloudFormation at deploy time into the WAF byte-match strings and the CloudFront custom header, so rotating either one takes a redeploy of both stacks, not just a new secret version.

The three consumer-config secrets are imported, not created: each gateway reads its own at runtime through getSecret with a 600-second cache and Zod-parses it. DVLA's holds the API key, username and password — they are used only inside the gateway Lambda.

d.tech: Rotation enabled on all three created keys
d.role: Encryption for flow logs, alarm topics and every Lambda's environment.
facts: Created: alias/flex-vpc-flow-logs-key and alias/flex-alerts-key in eu-west-2, alias/{stage}-flex-alerts-relay-key in us-east-1.

The fourth is imported, not created: /{env}/flex-param/secret/encryption-key encrypts the environment variables of every function built on the Flex* constructs, each of which is then granted decrypt on it.

Defect: that key is read with StringParameter.valueForStringParameter rather than BaseStack.import(), so it records no stack-dependency edge and gets no synth-time existence check — a missing parameter fails at deploy instead of at synth, unlike every other imported value.

The flow-log key grants only the write path to delivery.logs.amazonaws.com. No reader grant is written on top of CDK's default account-root kms:* statement, so decrypt is delegated to IAM rather than blocked outright.

nodes.label: S3 TLS enforcement
nodes.sub: CDK Aspect applied at App level

d.role: Denies non-TLS requests on every bucket in the app.
facts: Adds a Deny on s3:* for AnyPrincipal when aws:SecureTransport is false, covering both the bucket ARN and its objects.
Applied to the App, so a new bucket cannot be added without it — though it matches on instanceof Bucket, so an imported or L1 bucket would not be visited.

nodes.label: Log redaction
nodes.sub: a JSON replacer on every log line

d.role: Last line of defence between a handler and CloudWatch.
facts: 20 secret key patterns (token, authorization, card and CVV forms) and 17 PII key patterns (names, DOB, NINO, postcode, sort code) match on key names. Values are matched against a JWT prefix, email, UK phone, NINO, postcode and IPv4 patterns, plus a Luhn-checked card-number detector.
FLEX_LOG_PII_DEBUG can switch off the PII half — but never in production, where the check returns false unconditionally. FlexLogger.setLogLevel is a hard no-op in production for the same reason.
addSecretValue, addSensitiveKey and addSensitivePattern exist for runtime registration, with longest-first escaped alternation — but nothing in the repository calls them.

d.auth: None — this layer does not know who is asking
facts: Attached with webAclId. The default action is allow, so a request stops here only if a rule blocks it.

d.auth: Bearer token shape only, no signature check
d.carries: The Authorization header and the correlation id
facts: Associated with the default (API) behaviour. /docs* has its own function that only rewrites URIs, which is why documentation requests carry no correlation id.

d.protocol: Shield Advanced protection on the distribution ARN
d.carries: DDoS detection, plus automatic response in count mode
facts: Not created in the development environment, so ephemeral PR stages and personal stages run without it.

edges.label: HTTPS to the origin, carrying x-origin-verify

facts: Caching is disabled on this behaviour, so every request travels this hop.
OriginProtocolPolicy.HTTPS_ONLY here is CDK's HttpOrigin default rather than an explicit setting.

d.auth: Byte match on the origin secret
d.carries: Requests that carry the right header value
facts: Anything else meets the Web ACL's default block, including a request sent straight to the execute-api hostname.
One shared authorizer function in the platform stack, imported by ARN into each domain stack that has public routes.

d.protocol: HTTPS to cognito-idp, or to the stub Function URL in development
d.auth: None — the JWKS endpoint is public
d.carries: The signing keys used to verify the token
facts: There is no cognito-idp interface endpoint, so this call leaves the VPC through the NAT gateway from the egress tier.

d.protocol: IAM policy document returned to API Gateway
facts: The context arrives at the handler as ctx.auth.pairwiseId; if it is absent the SDK raises an authorization error inside the function rather than at the gateway.

d.carries: The request plus the one asserted claim

d.protocol: HTTPS through the API Gateway interface endpoint
d.auth: SigV4 signed with the function's own execution-role credentials
facts: Single attempt: retries are opt-in on flexFetch and nothing on this path opts in.

edges.label: caps every role in the stack

d.carries: The maximum permission any role in the stack may hold
facts: Effective permission is the intersection of the role's own policies and this boundary, so a mistaken inline grant cannot widen it.

d.protocol: AWS::IAM::Policy attached to the function role
d.carries: Only the route ARNs that route declares
facts: Applied only when the route lists integrations, so a route with none can invoke nothing on the private API at all.

rows: Lambda — every function, all three tiers
CloudWatch Logs · one group per function
Structured JSON from Powertools, passed through the @flex/logging sanitiser
httpMethod, ip, protocol, requestTime, resourcePath, responseLength, status, user, caller
Production only. loggingLevel: ERROR, dataTraceEnabled: false — no request or response bodies. Other stages set no method logging at all
Log group is production only, but loggingLevel: INFO is set in every stage, with dataTraceEnabled: false
S3 · flow-log bucket · plain text · 1-minute aggregation · ALL traffic
All default fields plus VPC id, subnet id, instance id, TCP flags, packet source and destination, flow direction
Requests to the OpenAPI spec bucket
Macie scan of the CloudFront access-log bucket
Would be: weekly Monday scan, 100% sampling, recommended managed identifiers
tables.note: Read the encryption column against itself: the flow-log bucket names a customer-managed key, the Lambda log groups and both S3 access-log buckets leave the property unset. The two execution log groups are created only when the stage is production, so in other stages API Gateway execution logging has no log group of its own.

tables.name: What the sanitiser removes before a log is written
rows: secret, token, password, passwd, authorization, apikey, api_key, credential, private / access / client keys, signing, card number, PAN, CVV, CVC, CSC, card security code, card verification, card expiry
Exact values registered at runtime via addSecretValue(), matched longest-first
email, phone, mobile, forename, surname, first / last / full name, date of birth, DOB, NINO, national insurance, postcode, zip code, sort code, account number, IP address
email address, UK phone number, National Insurance number, UK postcode, IPv4 address
tables.note: Matched values are replaced with ***REDACTED***. isPiiDebugEnabled() returns false when FLEX_ENVIRONMENT is production, before it reads the flag, and the flag is checked only after the secret patterns have run. All of it is in libs/logging/src/sanitizer.ts.

tables.name: Telemetry events written to the logs
tables.note: 21 events in libs/telemetry/src/events.ts as a zod enum, and 3 more in libs/telemetry/src/cff.ts — kept separate because the zod enum cannot be bundled into a CloudFront Function under its size limit. Every event is written as { level, message: "telemetry", telemetry: { event, details } }.

rows: Stack is written, but its instantiation is commented out in app.ts
tables.note: "None" means no construct in this repository creates it. Any of these may still be enabled at the AWS Organisation or account level, outside this codebase — this table describes the CDK app only.
